An explanation of how combat reloading (reloading with inventory closed) works:


Your load out is a set of pockets/loops on your vest. For this example you have 4 pockets and you have 4 mags in your load out, one in each pocket, and a fifth mag in the gun. 
You go to reload, your gun is in one hand, you grab the magazine in the gun with the other and remove it. You now have a gun in one hand and a magazine in the other. All four pockets have a magazine in them so you can't put the magazine in your hand into a pocket and you can't take a magazine out of a pocket because both of your hands are full. What do you do? 
Shove the magazine in your hand into your drop-pouch, or backpack since we don�t simulate a drop-pouch. 
Now you have a free hand, you take a magazine from a loadout pocket and put it into the gun. leaving you with one empty loadout pocket. Reload complete. 
If you start the process with a free pocket in your loadout the mag from the gun gets put into that pocket. Unless it is empty, then by default it goes into your bag. This can be changed so that empty magazines are placed into loadout slots or dropped to the ground.


If you have the inventory open then it is not a combat reload and an additional attempt to place the magazine into your load out is performed because it is assumed you can set the gun or magazine down. Also the setting to drop magazines on the ground is ignored when inventory is open. 
However if you think that RavenAscendant is wrong and that during a combat reload your stalker has a magical third hand to hold the magazine that came out of the gun until it can be placed in the freed up loadout slot, or that they would hold it in their teeth/knees/armpit/psionic powers, then there is an option below to enable that behavior.
Use a third hand to place an ejected magazine back into your loadout after a combat reload.
Raven still thinks this is wrong.

%c[pda_green]Mags Redux%c[ui_gray_1]
 
 
Welcome to using Mags Redux. This guide will cover most of the features and changes you can expect when using this mod. 
For users of the old Anomaly Magazines (from Wuut) you can expect little difference in gameplay. Most of the functionality is the same.
 

%c[pda_green]I. How to load and fire weapons%c[ui_gray_1]
 
� Weapons that would logically use magazines in real life require the usage of magazines. 
 � Weapons that do not will behave as in vanilla (shotguns, some bolt rifles, revolvers) 
� Ammo must be manually loaded into magazines. The magazine description will indicate what sort of ammo is compatible. To load ammo, drag the ammo item onto the magazine. This will initiate a loading procedure, which will one by one load rounds in. 
 � To cancel this procedure, click anywhere. 
� To put a magazine into loadout, right click the magazine. There will be an option 'add to loadout'. The magazine background will change color and an icon will be added: this means the magazine has been added to your equipment loadout. 
 � From here, if you are holding an eligible weapon, reloading your weapon will utilize the magazine in your loadout. 
 � The mod will attempt to automatically select the magazine that a) has the largest size and b) has a top round equal to your ammo type. 
� Magazines can also be manually inserted and ejected. Right click a weapon to find the option to eject the magazine. 
� Ammo wheel can be used to swap magazines. Magazines are categorized by the top round.
 

%c[pda_green]II. Where to find magazines%c[ui_gray_1]
 
� Vendors that stock guns will stock magazines. Magazines may also be sold to them for a pittance. 
� NPCs will have a couple magazines for their weapon, with a little ammo. 
 � NPCs, specifically high-rank NPCs, have a small chance of dropping improved magazines. These magazines load faster, have higher capacities, or both.


%c[pda_green]III. Explanation of MCM options.%c[ui_gray_1]
 
� Loot quality: Affects quantity of dropped mags, fill amount, and chance for improved magazines. 
� Load/unload time factor: Multiplier on the bullet load/unload speed in magazines. 
� Fast loading: Enables instant un/loading of magazines IN STASH ONLY. 
� One in the chamber: Preserves a chambered round when switching mags, just like real life.

40-round extended MP7 magazine modified to accept the 5.7x28mm round developed and manufactured by FN Herstal. Due to the somewhat rare nature of 4.6x30 rounds, some thrifty technicians were able to retrofit the MP7 to fire the same round as the FN P90 and Five Seven.
Standard 40-round MP7 magazine chambered for 4.6x30mm ammunition.
Standard-issue 12-round magazine for the Fort-12 handgun. Commonly seen in the Zone as the sidearm of backline Ukrainian Military troops or stalkers with backgrounds as police officers.
Fort-12 magazine modified to accept 9x19 Parabellum rounds.

A true oddity, this is a Colt 1911 magazine modified to take the much skinnier 7.62x25 Tokarev cartridge. Only the Russian variants of the 1911 popular among Dutyers are capable of accepting such a modification. Proponents of the modification argue that the improved controllability of a smaller round combined with the commonality of the ammo make for a much more reliable sidearm, especially with the 1911's robust design. Detractors say that it is an unnecessary and patriotically motivated luxury, especially when cheaper options like the CZ-52 handgun exist.
Standard-issue 13-round magazine for the Fort-17 handgun. Can be loaded into the older Fort-12 as well.
Fort-17 magazine modified to accept 9x19 Parabellum rounds at the cost of some capacity.
An extended magazine for the fully automatic version of the CZ 75 pistol. It's worth noting that it is fully interchangeable with its standard counterpart.
An extended magazine for a rechambered CZ 75 pistol with 20 round capacity.
A Yugoslavian model of the TT-33 magazine with extra ammo capacity of 1 bullet. Works with regular TT pistols as well, allowing them to carry an extra round ready.
A modified version of the EM-2's Magazine, instead of using its own proprietary .380 British, it uses 7.62x51mm NATO.
The magazine for the StG44 in 7.92x33 Kurzpatrone holds 30 rounds.
Standard magazine for the FG-42 sniper rifle, it holds 20 rounds of 7.62x57 ammunition.
Magazine for the DP-27 Machinegun, houses 47 rounds of 7.62x54r ammunition.
A magazine for the Grease Gun. Very crude and simple it seems.
Magazine for the MAC-10 sub machinegun, chambered in 9x19 parabellum, this magazine carries 32 rounds.
Magazine for the MAC-10 sub machinegun, chambered in 9x19 parabellum, this magazine carries 50 rounds.
Magazine for the M240B Light Machinegun, houses 100 rounds of .308 NATO(7.62x51) ammunition.
20-shell magazine for the Vepr-12. Despite their similarities, the Vepr cannot share magazines with the Saiga.
Standard magazine for the MAC 10 smg. Holds 30 rounds of .45 ACP ammunition. They run out quick with this gun's high rate of fire.
Modified 30-round magazine used in the MP9. Has been converted to fire 5.7x28.
Standard 9x19 30-round magazine used in the MP9. They are a lot more fun to dump, than to load.
Extended 33 round Glock magazine. Most useful for automatic Glock models, or pistol caliber carbines that accept Glock magazines.
Extended 33 round Glock magazine, modified to load 9x18. This allows a Glock to provide more firepower than many SMGs.
Custom .338 Lapua Magnum magazine for use with the experimental .338 SVDK. Very similar (though not compatible) to the magazine used in the SVCh-8.6.

Standard magazine for the FN High Power pistol. Despite the similar appearance, due to modifications allowing for the higher capacity, magazines for the High Power are incompatible with the original Hi-Power and vice-versa.

Modified magazine for the FN High Power pistol, rechambered for 9x18. Despite the similar appearance, due to modifications allowing for the higher capacity, magazines for the High Power are incompatible with the original Hi-Power and vice-versa.

Standard 30 round Thompson submachine gun magazine chambered in .45 acp. The Thompson is not a gun that many would expect to find in the zone, perhaps a gunsmith with peculiar tastes has been producing copies.

50-round Thompson magazine for the Thompson submachine gun. Normally the M1A1 pattern of Thompson possesses a different mag weld that does not accept drums, however, aftermarket modifications have made them compatible.
30 round magazine for the custom M1A1 Carbine. As part of modifications from 5.7x33 spitfire parts to this current carbine, adjustments were made to facilitate the reliable feeding of 5.7x28.

Standard 32 round Sten Magazine. These magazines were notorious for their unreliability, an issue further exacerbated by a tendency of some users to use the magazine as a grip. An overly tight grip on the magazine or the magazine well could cause deformation and reliability issues and should be avoided.

Standard 32 round Sa 24/26 Magazine. Unlike many other magazines for the bottlenecked 7.62x25 round that are noticeably curved, these magazines are straight, lending them to be used in some 7.62x25 conversions for some SMGs.
Belt for the MG42, holds 100 rounds. No box, drape it over your shoulder and hope it doesn't get caught on something.
